land.text: the Chouf, the Druze mountain of the Maan emirs, in the Mamluk Sultanate's Syria until the Ottoman conquest of 1516-1517

predecessors.note: The page gives 'Fakhr al-Din I (1516-1544)' as first emir; the Ottoman conquest of Syria and Egypt is not on the pages opened. Cliopatria carries the Chouf in its Mamluk Sultanate shape until 1518 and its Ottoman Empire shape afterwards.

The page gives no area; Latakia is 'tax farms reached as far north as'. The Hauran and Palmyra are not on the page.

region.text: the Chouf and Mount Lebanon around Baakleen

ledger.note: 1516: the Maan emirate of the Chouf begins under Fakhr al-Din I. The page lists 'Fakhr al-Din I (1516-1544)' and says the Maan family rose in the early sixteenth century; Baakleen the capital (1516-1600). The page gives no founding event.

region.text: the Sidon and Beirut nahiyas, Matn, Jurd, the southern Beqaa and parts of Jabal Amil

ledger.note: 14 July 1589: Fakhr al-Din II's tax farms of Sidon and Beirut. He 'held the iltizam of the Sidon and Beirut nahiyas and the port of Beirut from 14 July 1589'; 1591-1594 his farms 'extended over the Chouf, Matn, Jurd, southern Beqaa Valley, and parts of Jabal Amil'.

region.text: the nahiyas of Acre, Tiberias and Safed

ledger.note: July 1602: Safed, Tiberias and Acre. 'Shortly before July 1602 he gained the iltizam of the Acre, Tiberias, and Safed nahiyas. In July 1602 he became sanjak-bey of Safed' (the Emirate page says 1598).
1606: Keserwan. 'He joined the Kurdish rebel Ali Janbulad against Yusuf Sayfa in 1606 and took over Keserwan.'
1623: the Beqaa after Anjar. 'After his victory at the Battle of Anjar in 1623, he extended control into the Beqaa Valley'; the Sultan gave him the title 'Sultan of the Mountain'.
1626: Salamiyah, Hama and Homs. 'He later captured Salamiyah (1626), then Hama and Homs, and placed his deputies in them.'

region.text: Tripoli and its eyalet, with the coast to Latakia

ledger.note: c. 1627: Tripoli and the coast to Latakia. He 'gained practical control of Tripoli and its eyalet, and his tax farms reached as far north as Latakia'; beylerbey of Tripoli in 1627 according to one source, which the Aleppine historian does not confirm.

region.text: the conquests of 1602-1627 beyond Mount Lebanon: Galilee, the Beqaa, Hama, Homs, Tripoli and Ajlun

ledger.note: 1633: Kucuk Ahmed Pasha takes Fakhr al-Din. The Ottomans appointed him to Damascus in 1632 'with the aim of eliminating him'; 'the lead gives 1633 for the siege and surrender'; Fakhr al-Din was beheaded in Constantinople on 13 April 1635 (infobox). The conquests beyond the mountain pass back to the Ottoman governors.
1697: the Shihab emirs succeed the Maan. 'Haydar al-Shihab (chosen in 1697)' after Ahmad, 'the last male of the line'; the emirate continues as an iltizam under the Shihabs.

region.text: Wadi al-Taym, the Beqaa and Jabal Amil

ledger.note: c. 1799: fiscal authority over the Beqaa and Jabal Amil. 'After the Acre crisis, an Ottoman decree gave him fiscal authority over Mount Lebanon, Wadi al-Taym, the Beqaa Valley, and Jabal Amil'; the page gives no exact date and says he 'had little actual control over these lands'.
1821: the Beqaa conquered. 'His forces conquered the Beqaa Valley under his son Khalil.' The page does not name the previous holders.

region.text: Jabal Amil, Koura, Sidon and Beirut

ledger.note: 1832: Muhammad Ali enlarges Bashir's jurisdiction. In the Egyptian conquest of Syria that began 1 October 1831, 'Muhammad Ali extended his jurisdiction to Jabal Amil, Koura, and the port cities of Sidon and Beirut'; Acre fell to the Egyptians on 21 May 1832.

region.text: Jabal Amil, Koura and the ports of Beirut, Sidon and Tyre

ledger.note: 25 September 1840: allied forces take Beirut, Sidon and Tyre. After the sheikhs' rebellion of 27 May and the bombardment of Beirut from 11 September, 'allied forces captured Beirut, Sidon, Haifa, and Tyre'; the sultan replaced Bashir on 8 October and he surrendered on 11 October. The Egyptian-granted districts return to Ottoman governors.

region.text: Mount Lebanon, the Shuf, Kisrawan and the Matn

ledger.note: January 1842: the Shihab emirate ends. 'In January 1842, the sultan withdrew the appointment, and Bashir III went into exile in Constantinople'; on 7 December 1842 the Porte divided Mount Lebanon into a Christian and a Druze qaimaqamate under the governor of Sidon.

wars.name: Fakhr al-Din II against the Ottoman governors

zones.text: the Beqaa, Hama, Homs, Tripoli, Galilee and Ajlun

wars.outcome: 1623: he beat Mustafa Pasha at Anjar in the Beqaa and became 'Sultan of the Mountain'; 1632 Kucuk Ahmed Pasha was sent to Damascus; his son Ali was killed near Khan Hasbaya; he surrendered in 1633 and was beheaded in 1635.
wars.note: The lead of the page gives 1633 for the siege; his exile in Tuscany and Sicily was 1613-1618 (Sidon blockaded 16 September 1613; back at Acre 29 September 1618).

wars.name: Ottoman punitive expedition against Milhim Shihab
wars.outcome: An Ottoman punitive expedition against Milhim in 1748; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: No change of frontier on the page.

wars.name: Bashir II against Jazzar Pasha
wars.outcome: In 1789, pursued by Cezzar Ahmed Pasha of Acre, Bashir defeated his forces in the Bekaa; Jazzar 'had been acquiring Shihab territory'; relations soured again in 1799 over a troop levy during the siege of Acre; Jazzar died in 1804.
wars.note: Jazzar had backed Bashir's accession in 1789 (Bashir II page). Counterpart is the Acre pashalik, successor of Daher al-Umar's sheikhdom (the sheikhdom-of-acre dossier ends in 1776); a Jazzar/Sidon Eyalet dossier does not exist.

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1831-1833)
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Pasha's forces began the conquest of Syria on 1 October 1831; Bashir offered his allegiance; Acre fell on 21 May 1832; Bashir's troops under Khalil helped take Damascus (16 June) and beat the Ottoman army at Homs (9 July); Muhammad Ali enlarged Bashir's jurisdiction in 1832.
wars.note: The war article itself was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Oriental Crisis of 1840
wars.outcome: 27 May 1840: Mount Lebanon's sheikhs rebel against Bashir and Ibrahim Pasha; 11 September allied naval bombardment of Beirut; 25 September Beirut, Sidon, Haifa and Tyre taken; 8 October the sultan replaces Bashir; he surrenders 11 October and goes to Malta.
wars.note: The crisis article itself was not opened (page budget).

certainty.note: An iltizam (tax-farm) territory with no described boundary: the Chouf core is firm, the Beqaa, Jabal Amil and the 1623-1633 conquests are the approximate part; the fiscal authority of c. 1799 was largely nominal.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (Mount Lebanon sits inside its Ottoman Empire shape; Lebanon 1944-2024 is a separate row). Written by me-10-x; 3 pages opened (budget up to 5). Not opened: the Maan dynasty and Shihab dynasty articles, Qaimaqamate, the war articles of 1831-33 and 1840, and any page for the Mamluk-Ottoman change of 1516-1517 (predecessor given as mamluk-sultanate by the researcher's reading). The Emirate page gives Fakhr al-Din I as 1516-1544 and no founding event, so confidence on the 1516 found event is 2. Page conflicts: the Sanjak of Safed 1598 (Emirate) vs July 1602 (Fakhr al-Din); Sidon-Beirut sanjak-bey December 1593 vs December 1592; Bashir II's accession 1788 vs September 1789; early Shihab reign dates (the page's own list conflicts). Yusuf Shihab 'aided the Mamluk invasion of 1770 and briefly occupied Damascus' (Emirate page) is not recorded as an event because the Ali Bey pages give Damascus to the Egyptians and Daher in June 1771. The Hasbaya and Rashaya emirs are not on the pages. A Jazzar / Sidon Eyalet dossier would be the counterpart for the post-1775 Acre pashalik. Places by lon/lat radius: the Chouf, Western Beqaa, Keserwan, Salamiyah, Ajlun, Tiberias, Safed.
